course_name_original: Simulación numérica de componentes y estructuras
course_name_en: Numerical Simulation of Components and Structures

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and use of the principles of strength of materials
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of industrial installations
Applied knowledge of metallic and reinforced concrete structures
Ability to handle mandatory specifications, regulations, and standards
That students can transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis, and processing within their field of application
Develop the ability to work in a team
Ability to apply knowledge to practice

syllabus_topics: Introduction to numerical simulation of materials, components, and structures. The finite element method. FE programs today. Stages for an FE analysis: Preprocessing, analysis, and postprocessing. Types of problems in FE.
Preprocessing stage-I. Geometry generation. Parts and assemblies. Types of contacts between parts. Importing geometry from other programs.
Preprocessing stage-II. Part meshing. Element types. Meshing strategies. Meshing examples.
Preprocessing stage-III. Material definition: elasticity and plasticity. Definition of boundary conditions: types of contacts and joints.
Numerical simulation of linear problems. Analysis and postprocessing stage. Result extraction. Application examples.
Numerical simulation of nonlinear problems. Plasticity. Friction contacts. Application examples.
Numerical simulation of coupled thermo-mechanical problems. Application examples.
Introduction to the simulation of dynamic problems. Implicit and explicit calculation. Impact simulation. Application examples.
Introduction to the simulation of large deformation problems. Simulation of a rolling process. Simulation of a bending process.
Simulation of industrial structures. Matrix calculation programs. Calculation of industrial building structures. Application examples.
teaching_methods: Notes, tutorials and documentation included in the UBUVirtual platform
Finite element programs with educational license
Completion and presentation of assignments and evaluation tests

assessment_methods.method: Development and presentation of Assignment I
Development and presentation of Assignment II

assessment_rules: The evaluation system for exchange students must consider the case where the academic calendars of the home and host universities do not coincide. The weights are 20% for knowledge tests, 40% for Assignment I, and 40% for Assignment II. Students with exceptional evaluation must attend the established tests but may be excused from attending theoretical and practical classes.
